LESSON: NUTRITIVE VALUE OF FOODS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HOME SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Food and Nutrition
Topic 1.4: Nutritive Value of Foods
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nutritive Value of Foods, part of Food and Nutrition in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 HOME SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does knowledge of food nutrients promote healthy eating habits? 2. Why does the food you choose to eat affect your health?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nutritive Value of Foods together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learners speak engagingly, using facts, examples and visual aids to support their

points as they present on the classification of food nutrients.

● Learning to Learn: as learners search for information on food groups.

Values:
● Patriotism: the learners display awareness of their culture as they appreciate the use of locally available foods when

formulating meal plans

● Respect: the learners display acceptance by understanding and appreciating foods from other communities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health Promotion Issues: the learner gains knowledge in health and recognises the importance of food nutrients in the

prevention of nutritional deficiency diseases.
